attempts.raw_response: Her eyes, wide with a terrifying clarity, locked onto his. The air between them crackled, not with fear, but with a volatile recognition that silenced the jeering crowd. McLean’s men shifted uncomfortably, their weapons lowering slightly as they sensed the shift in power dynamics. He didn’t struggle against the ropes; instead, he tilted his head, offering her a faint, knowing smirk. It was a challenge, an invitation to remember who he truly was beneath the gag and the rough hemp. She took a step forward, the gravel crunching under her boot, her hand hovering near the holster at her hip. The shot had been anger, yes, but this moment demanded something sharper, colder. She wasn’t here to save him from strangers; she was here to settle a score with the man who had betrayed her trust.

pair.human_continuation:
Suddenly a
thing she had said jestingly to him one day came back with startling
force: "You must take Angels on trust." Of course you must! She was his
Angel. She must have seen! His life, and what was far more, her own, was
in her hands. There was nothing he could do but trust her. Surely she
was working out some plan.

The Angel knelt beside his flower bed and recklessly tore up by the
roots a big bunch of foxfire.

"These stems are so tough and sticky," she said. "I can't break them.
Loan me your knife," she ordered Freckles.

As she reached for the knife, her back was for one second toward the
men. She looked into his eyes and deliberately winked.
pair.prefix:
Would
she throw herself at the man's feet before them all? Couldn't she give
him even one thought? Hadn't she seen that he was gagged and bound? Did
she truly think that these were McLean's men? Why, she could not! It was
only a few days ago that she had been close enough to this man and angry
enough with him to peel the hat from his head with a shot!
